# QuickStark setup

Prepare or verify only the selected project. Inspect existing configuration before editing and preserve project conventions.

## Behavior

1. Resolve the repository root and read its agent instructions.
2. Detect the issue tracker, documentation conventions, test commands, release workflow, and existing QuickStark configuration.
3. Ask only for a material choice that cannot be inferred safely.
4. Create or repair the minimum project-owned configuration needed for the confirmed workflow.
5. Run targeted validation and report actual readiness.

Never create remote resources, credentials, releases, or deployments unless separately requested. Setup ends after configuration verification; it does not start planning or implementation.

## Modes

- Quick: verify the existing configuration and report the first blocking gap.
- Standard: verify and safely repair the normal project configuration.
- Deep: include wider integration and documentation checks without expanding project scope.

## Conditional project references

For a confirmed tracker, read only its adapter: [GitHub](issue-tracker-github.md), [GitLab](issue-tracker-gitlab.md), or [local Markdown](issue-tracker-local.md). Read [triage-labels.md](triage-labels.md) only when configuring an existing triage workflow, and [domain.md](domain.md) when domain documentation exists or terminology affects setup. Use verified project conventions rather than imposing the examples. These references describe formats and operations; loading them never authorizes issue creation, claiming, comments, closing, or another public workflow.

## Completion report and next steps

Keep one conversation checklist of meaningful stages: pending, active, verified, skipped, blocked or failed. One stage suffices for a short task. Check off only verified stages, supported by artifacts, commands, sources or observed behavior; explain skips and reopen invalidated evidence.

During long operations, aim for updates within sixty seconds when control returns. State the stage, observed progress or waiting, and needed input; running and elapsed time alone prove no progress or completion. Finish with what changed/configured or was found read-only, actual passed/failed checks, limitations and remaining work. All effort/report modes retain blockers and failed checks; never imply mutations in a read-only run.

Report at start, transitions, material changes, blockers, resumption and completion: Stage: <name> | Stage estimate: ~<N>% | Overall estimate: ~<N>% | <state> — <observed progress or waiting>. Input needed: <none or exact need>. Overall covers this bounded root, or the entire explicitly submitted goal; a completed root does not complete its larger goal.

Assign meaningful stage effort weights initially. Overall = sum(weight × stage estimate) / sum(in-scope weights). Estimate from verified milestones, observed partial work and remaining effort, never counts of checklist items, elapsed time, tokens or a running process. Use coarse whole percentages and explain low confidence. Keep weights stable; explain changed scope/decomposition, recalibration, reopened checks and decreases. Out-of-scope skips lose their weight with no credit; already-satisfied in-scope work earns credit only from current evidence and keeps its weight. Helpers contribute evidence without public reports or double-counting.

While waiting or blocked, retain the last defensible estimate unless evidence changes; state the required input/event. Preserve scope, weights, estimates and revision-bound evidence for resumption. Reuse valid progress without resetting or counting twice; reopen invalidated checks. Stage 100% requires verified stage completion; overall 100% requires every acceptance criterion and required check for the stated scope. Cap unverified coarse estimates at 95%. Failed required checks, unresolved criteria and actionable P0/P1 findings prevent completion regardless of percentages; status and verification gates prevail.
